speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked	 the Minister for Foreign Affairs what are the Ministry's plans to reinforce a common ASEAN position on the South China Sea issue in light of the recent joint statement by China, Brunei, Cambodia and Laos in view of the fact that Singapore is currently the ASEAN-China dialogue partnership coordinator.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I hope Members will appreciate that I have to be extra careful in my reply.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Chair, Lao PDR, had emphasised that all 10 ASEAN Foreign Ministers remained seriously concerned over the recent and ongoing developments in the South China Sea and reaffirmed the need to enhance mutual trust and confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In addition, there is a need for all stakeholders to exercise self-restraint in their conduct of activities and to pursue peaceful resolution of disputes in accordance with international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This sentiment was most recently conveyed by the ASEAN Foreign Ministers during the Special ASEAN-China Foreign Ministers' Meeting which we held in Kunming, China, on 14 June.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We had a very frank and robust exchange of views on issues of mutual interest, including the situation in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The media attention that occurred after that meeting on the failure to issue an ASEAN Joint Press Statement, in fact, reflects the importance that the international community places on ASEAN's unity and the developments in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The 49th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting is scheduled in two weeks' time and I am sure this issue will arise again.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Page: 42 On our part, I just want to emphasise that Singapore is not currently the Chairman of ASEAN and we are also, very importantly, not a claimant state in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have consistently stated that Singapore takes no position on the merits of the specific territorial claims, and the Philippines' arbitration proceedings against China was a national decision undertaken by the Philippines without consultation with the rest of us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore's position on this matter has been clearly articulated in January 2013 by my predecessor, Minister K Shanmugam, here in Parliament.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In brief, our position is that the overlapping sovereignty claims in the South China Sea should be settled by the parties concerned.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, this should be done in accordance with international law, including the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: All parties should refrain from provocative behaviour that could raise tensions in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Territorial claims could be resolved by negotiations, adjudication or arbitration.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Six-Point Principles on the South China Sea that was adopted by ASEAN in 2012 clearly states that ASEAN supports the peaceful settlement of disputes, in accordance with international law, including the 1982 UNCLOS.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, seven out of the 10 ASEAN Member States have used adjudication and/or arbitration to resolve disputes in the past.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN, at the highest levels, has also consistently reaffirmed the principle that disputes should be settled peacefully, with full respect for legal and diplomatic processes, and this was most recently issued by our Leaders in the Sunnylands Declaration after the Special ASEAN-US Leaders' Summit in February 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have made some, albeit slow, progress in confidence-building and conflict-prevention measures.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the recent ASEAN-China Senior Officials' Meetings on the Implementation of the DOC that were co-chaired by Singapore and China, we adopted the MFA-to-MFA hotline for maritime emergencies, which will be manned on a 24/7 basis.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This hotline will help build confidence amongst parties to the DOC and, hopefully, help prevent ground accidents.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also started preliminary discussions on a proposed Code for Unplanned Encounters at Sea (CUES), to be applied in the South China Sea, on which I had previously briefed Members.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope that the observance of CUES will send a positive signal and help manage the situation at sea and prevent miscalculations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our officials have also begun looking at possible elements of the Code of Conduct but, quite frankly, this will take time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Progress has been extremely slow on this front.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As the country coordinator for ASEAN-China dialogue relations and as the co-chair of the DOC process, Singapore will continue to work closely with all stakeholders to advance ASEAN unity, credibility and centrality.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Page: 43 Secondly, what would be Singapore's stand on the expected ruling?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, if China does, indeed, not abide by the ruling of the Permanent Court of Arbitration, as it declared earlier, what would be Singapore's reaction to that?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First, we will have to see what the ruling is tomorrow.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am not privy to it and I think all of us, all stakeholders and all interested parties, will have to study it in great detail.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I cannot at this point in time give an answer with any certainty on whether there will be a joint ASEAN statement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It depends on the ruling, the respective analysis and assessments by the sovereign countries and whether there is a consensus.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we will have to wait and see.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am going to be quite busy for the next few days.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have no overlapping claims with any ASEAN member in the South China Sea.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We believe in a peaceful resolution of disputes and, as I have said earlier in my answer, including negotiations, adjudication or arbitration.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the case of Singapore, we have, on more than one occasion, used adjudication or arbitration to successfully settle disagreements.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The other question on what will we do if China does not comply, I will consider that to be a hypothetical question and, with due respect, I do not wish to engage in speculation at this point.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As for the Member's fourth supplementary question on military activities, I would say I have addressed it earlier on.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The key point is to reduce tensions and to look for peaceful resolution of differences.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We believe this is still possible and we hope that cooler heads will prevail.
